pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - run examples in wasm in CI
pr_body:
# Objective

- Run examples in WASM in CI
- Fix #4817 

## Solution

- on feature `bevy_ci_testing`
  - add an extra log message before exiting
  - when building for wasm, read CI config file at compile time
- add a simple [playwright](https://playwright.dev) test script that opens the browser then waits for the success log, and takes a screenshot
- add a CI job that runs the playwright test for Chromium and Firefox on one example (lighting) and save the screenshots
  - Firefox screenshot is good (with some clusters visible)
  - Chromium screenshot is gray, I don't know why but it's logging `GPU stall due to ReadPixels`
  - Webkit is not enabled for now, to revisit once https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=234926 is fixed or worked around
- the CI job only runs on bors validation

example run: https://github.com/mockersf/bevy/actions/runs/2361673465. The screenshots can be downloaded
pr_comments: * added more examples. now running examples `shapes`, `lighting`, `ui` in CI (so 2d, 3d and ui) * chrome has a good screenshot for all but `lighting` * tried enabling webkit, it's not able to start a webgl2 render context in CI * shorten the number of frames per example to run faster * example run with hot cache: https://github.com/mockersf/bevy/actions/runs/2362569845 biggest place to gain time would be install wasm-bindgen which could be shorten by using [cargo-quickinstall](https://github.com/alsuren/cargo-quickinstall) if everyone is ok with using that in CI

The run-examples step is now the longest by quite a bit (16 minutes vs 9 minutes for check-unused-dependencies); could we split it up into a couple of different jobs by platform perhaps?

I'd be open to `cargo-quickinstall` if there are appreciable speed gains.

> The run-examples step is now the longest by quite a bit (16 minutes vs 9 minutes for check-unused-dependencies); could we split it up into a couple of different jobs by platform perhaps?

the 16 minutes `run-examples` job is only running linux. With this PR we would run examples:
* on linux on all commits (16 minutes without cache / 14 minutes with)
* on windows on bors actions (validation and merging in main) (20 minutes without cache, 14 minutes with cache)
* on wasm on bors actions (validation and merging in main) (10 minutes with cache, I think, don't have a run without cache on hands)

This is failing, so I'm pulling this out for now.

bors r-
We couldn't have asked for a better justification for merging this PR ASAP 😆

Pull request successfully merged into main.

issue_context.title: Run examples for WASM in CI
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

As seen in #4811 and #4813, WebAssembly examples don't always behave the same as on other platforms.

This is particularly true for audio, asset loading, windowing and rendering.

Web is an important platform for Bevy, and accidentally breaking it is far too easy.

## What solution would you like?

Run at least some of the examples as a check in our continuous integration pipeline, targeting the web platform.

## What alternative(s) have you considered?

Use Gitpod or an equivalent (#4700) to enable devs to easily manually check that web examples are working during risky PRs.

review_comments: Is this still true? You said that you couldn't get webkit working.
Yes! the CLI can run on all three browsers, but it won't work on webkit in CI. Still, it can run on your local setup
I wonder if we should be setting some custom property on `window` instead. That way we're not relying on the fairly large number of assumptions that mean `info` lands in the console.
if you think the other way around, this is also a test that logs lands in the console
Again, should this be a custom property on document/window?
I don't think you can `include_str` something not a string literal?
I mean sure? But you can read a string which isn't a string literal. We don't do anything special with this string that requires it to be statically inlined in the WASM blob.
I'm not sure I understand what you mean? You don't have access to the file system in wasm.

Why would we need file system access to read the config values?

They would be assigned onto the window object as a string or object

I looked a little into how to add those to to the javascript window object, it could work but mean that the file would be read from typescript, and I don't want to start reading ron files in typescript. And I would prefer to keep the same file format as the other example runs
This should be fixed somehow but I would rather get the benefits of running wasm examples sooner than later and this doesn’t really seem trivial to fix in a good way.
